To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the automatic construction of discourse structures is possible and that the resulting structures can be used for summarizing text.

(1) discourse parsing and summarization can be done successfully without any semantic analysis of the input text and (2) the performance of a system that uses a discourse based summarization method to identify the most important parts in a text can be very close to that of humans.
the use of non-semantic discourse structures in summarization is feasible, and that such structures can be used to improve performance in summarization.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the automatic extraction of information from large collections of texts, and the automatic generation of texts that contain information that was not present in the original texts.
the automatic analysis and synthesis of texts.
the development of methods for the automatic analysis and synthesis of discourse structures in natural language.

the discourse structure of a text can be automatically derived by a computational method that uses no linguistic knowledge other than the meanings of words and the syntactic structures of sentences.

it is possible to construct automatic discourse parsers and summarizers that are both effective and efficient.
